title: Try registering a `chooseOpsMethod()` for a stepper
description:
CC @hadley @t-kalinowski @ltierney - This is an example of testing out `chooseOpsMethod()` to prove that it works as expected. And it looks good to me!

I think we will actually end up registering `chooseOpsMethod.vctrs_vctr()`, which will handle it correctly for _all_ vctrs subclasses, like this almanac stepper. So I won't end up merging this.

The only problem that can come up is if _both_ classes register a `chooseOpsMethod()` method with conflicting `mx` and `my` methods, like what I do below by registering a method for `<Date>`. That can result in _silent_ weird results, which is a little scary, but I still think this feature is a big improvement.

Before (R 4.2):

``` r
library(almanac)

# A Friday
x <- as.Date("2023-04-21")

# Boo
x + workdays(1)
#> Warning: Incompatible methods ("+.Date", "+.vctrs_vctr") for "+"
#> [1] "2023-04-22"

workdays(1) + x
#> Warning: Incompatible methods ("+.vctrs_vctr", "+.Date") for "+"
#> <stepper[1]>
#> [1] 19469

x - workdays(1)
#> Warning: Incompatible methods ("-.Date", "-.vctrs_vctr") for "-"
#> [1] "2023-04-20"

workdays(1) - x
#> Warning: Incompatible methods ("-.vctrs_vctr", "-.Date") for "-"
#> <stepper[1]>
#> [1] -19467
```

After (r-devel):

``` r
library(almanac)

# A Friday
x <- as.Date("2023-04-21")

# Yay! ("steps" over the weekend)
x + workdays(1)
#> [1] "2023-04-24"

workdays(1) + x
#> [1] "2023-04-24"

x - workdays(1)
#> [1] "2023-04-20"

# Correct!
workdays(1) - x
#> Error in `vec_arith()` at vctrs/R/type-vctr.R:659:4:
#> ! <stepper> - <date> is not permitted


# Let's try also registering a method for Date
chooseOpsMethod.Date <- function(x, y, mx, my, cl, reverse) {
  TRUE
}

# Boo
# - Silently uses the `.Date` method because it found it "first"
# - `workdays(1)` is stored as `1` plus attributes internally, so it is the same as `+ 1`
x + workdays(1)
#> [1] "2023-04-22"

# - Silently uses the `.almanac_stepper` method because it found it "first"
workdays(1) + x
#> [1] "2023-04-24"
```

<sup>Created on 2023-04-19 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

title: Lazily register `slider_plus()` and `slider_minus()` methods
description:
Joint PR with https://github.com/DavisVaughan/slider/pull/184

- [x] Bump required slider version in DESCRIPTION to CRAN version
- [x] Bump required slider version in skip_if_not_installed() to CRAN version
- [x] Remove slider Remote

It is beautiful:

``` r
i <- as.Date("1970-01-07") + 0:7
x <- clock::as_weekday(i)

slider::slide_index(
  .x = x,
  .i = i,
  .f = identity,
  .before = almanac::workdays(1),
  .after = almanac::workdays(1)
)
#> [[1]]
#> <weekday[2]>
#> [1] Wed Thu
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> <weekday[3]>
#> [1] Wed Thu Fri
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> <weekday[5]>
#> [1] Thu Fri Sat Sun Mon
#> 
#> [[4]]
#> <weekday[4]>
#> [1] Fri Sat Sun Mon
#> 
#> [[5]]
#> <weekday[4]>
#> [1] Fri Sat Sun Mon
#> 
#> [[6]]
#> <weekday[5]>
#> [1] Fri Sat Sun Mon Tue
#> 
#> [[7]]
#> <weekday[3]>
#> [1] Mon Tue Wed
#> 
#> [[8]]
#> <weekday[2]>
#> [1] Tue Wed
```

title: Cache fix
description:
Closes #6.

- The cache now uses the minimum `since` date, or minimum `rdate` as the `from` date to always call `ruleset.between()` with.
- Because of this, we can cache all dates between `since` and `to`, since they are computed along the way anyways. This significantly speeds up any time you call `sch_seq()` then again with a `to` date that is less than the first time.
- This change also fixes the problem with the cache not working right for disjoint date ranges, since we always cache a continuous range from `since` -> `to`.
- And we simplify the get/set parts of the cache by going back to just storing the dates, not the numerics. `unclass()` with altrep will take care of making less copies.
